chunks: There are some men who worship God only from the margin. If there is some profit they are content; but if calamity befalls them they turn about, thus losing both this world and the next. This is indeed a palpable loss.

key_terms.اطْمَأَنَّ: To be calm, content, or at ease.
key_terms.الْخُسْرَانُ الْمُبِينُ: The clear, evident, and manifest loss.
key_terms.انقَلَبَ عَلَىٰ وَجْهِهِ: To turn upside down; a metaphor for sudden reversal of state due to distress.
key_terms.حَرْفٍ: Edge, margin, or corner; implying a superficial or conditional stance.
key_terms.فِتْنَةٌ: Tribulation, trial, or calamity that tests faith.

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to worship God means when He says people worship Him 'on a corner' or 'margin'?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the term 'harf' (edge) signifies a faith lacking deep-rooted certainty, making the believer's state volatile and dependent on external circumstances. This verse highlights the fragility of conditional devotion, where the loss of worldly ease equates to the loss of spiritual stability, resulting in a 'manifest loss' of both dunya and akhirah. It serves as a warning against superficial piety that crumbles under the test of adversity.
